message: StaffMemberDrawer.tsx now renders the Employment Type row via transformAssignmentCategoryGroup(assignmentCategoryGroup, t) instead of the hardcoded pendingField placeholder, but StaffMemberDrawer.test.tsx has no assertion on this row for either a populated or null assignmentCategoryGroup. A regression that reverts this line to pendingField would not be caught by any test.

MpdAssignmentCategoryGroupEnum is mapped to display labels in two places: the new transformAssignmentCategoryGroup helper and the filter panel MenuItem children. The repo rule is one enum value maps to one label, so the dropdown and the row/drawer can drift apart on the next copy change.

transformAssignmentCategoryGroup already returns early for null/undefined, so the trailing default branch is unreachable for every value the type allows. It converts a future schema enum member from a compile error into a silent em dash in the UI.
dismissalDetail: the default branch is a deliberate runtime fallback for server enum values the client doesn't know yet; the unreachable-branch defect is gone (the early null return was removed) and helpers.test.ts covers the unknown-value path

message: The test is named "omits assignmentCategoryGroup" but it asserts the variable is sent as an explicit null, so it does not actually prove the argument is omitted.

Test is named 'omits assignmentCategoryGroup until an employment type is chosen' but the assertion checks that the variable is sent with value null, not that the key is omitted from the operation — the name and the behavior it verifies do not match.
The JSDoc comment on transformAssignmentCategoryGroup only restates the function name/signature and adds no non-obvious why, which this repo has repeatedly asked reviewers to trim.

The repo keeps localized enum-label helpers as getLocalizedX in src/lib/functions; this one is named transformAssignmentCategoryGroup and lives in a feature helpers file. Harmless today because the enum is used only here, but it makes the helper hard to find if a second feature needs the same label.

pendingField is documented as "Stands in for fields managedStaff cannot supply yet", but it is now also the placeholder for a field the API does supply as null. Grepping pendingField no longer tells you which fields are still unimplemented.

The MpdGoalAdmin gotcha note still says an empty cohort list means no cohorts exist at all, not that this user has none, and that the context auto-selects the first cohort whenever the list is non-empty. This PR makes coordinators see a role-filtered list (trainingSize > 0), so a coordinator can now get an empty list while cohorts do exist team-wide — the doc no longer matches the code it describes.

This adds a second empty state for the same situation the existing No Training Selected state (PR #2013) was built for, and they act differently: the new one hides the Training selector, the old one keeps it disabled. For coordinators the old branch can no longer be reached, so its comment is now stale, and admins with zero cohorts still get the old copy and layout.
noVisibleCohorts explicitly guards on !cohortsLoading and !cohortsError so the empty-state message does not flash during load or replace a real error, but no test in the diff exercises either guard.
Added inline comment restates what the ternary already shows (replacing CohortBar/ActiveGoalsContent with NullStateBox) rather than explaining a non-obvious why beyond the one useful clause.

The role check waits on userLoading but ignores a GetUser error. If that query fails, isGoalsAdmin comes back false, so an admin gets the coordinator-filtered list and may see a misleading message that cohorts do not include staff in their ministry.

The cohorts memo now filters non-admins to trainingSize > 0, but no test covers a coordinator whose selected cohort disappears from the filtered list after a re-render (e.g. attendees reassigned away mid-session), which is the scenario the useEffect's stale-selection fallback exists for.

Gating the cohort list on GetUser `loading` means the list is emptied and the page shows the loading state on every mount (and any GetUser refetch) even when the user is already cached, because the watchQuery default is cache-and-network with notifyOnNetworkStatusChange. The role is already known from cache at that point, so this adds a network round trip of blank page for no reason.
